name: The Inquisition
about: A pious lord's confessor starts hunting heretics. His fires spread from village herbwives to a great house's own people, and then to the King's court. Rein in the Faith and be called godless, or let it burn and see who it burns next.
title: The Inquisition

new.name: Brother {first}
new.memory: The gods showed me the rot in this realm, and gave me fire to burn it out.

goal.text: Burn the heresy out of every house, however high

beats.speaker: inquisitor
beats.text: {inquisitor}, confessor to {patron}, burns a herbwife in {pyre}'s market for talking to the dead. Before she dies she names the women of {accused}'s household as her customers.

court.text: {accused} of {accused.house}: "A mad friar is burning women in my own town, Your Grace, and now he wants my household. Rein him in."

options.label: Ban the Faith's trials in {pyre}
options.result: The King's order bans the friar's trials in {pyre}. That night {inquisitor} preaches about kings who protect witches.

options.label: Send royal judges to try every charge (100 gold)
options.hint: the King's law decides, not the friar
options.result: Royal judges ride for {pyre}, with orders that nobody burns without the King's seal.

options.label: Let the Faith try its heretics
options.result: {inquisitor} has the King's permission. He builds a bigger pyre.

beats.speaker: inquisitor
beats.text: Banned from {pyre}, {inquisitor} preaches in every other town instead. The crowds grow, and his sermons call the King the heretics' protector.

beats.speaker: inquisitor
beats.text: Under torture, {accused}'s steward confesses to everything they ask: the herbwife, the black candles, a goat in the cellar. {inquisitor} demands that {accused} answer for {accused.his} household.

court.text: {patron} of {patron.house}: "The confession is sworn, Your Grace. If a great lord can protect witches, anyone can. Hand {accused} to the Faith."

options.label: Throw out the confession, because it came from torture
options.result: The King's judges free the steward, or what's left of him. {inquisitor} curses the court from the steps.

options.label: Let the Faith try {accused}
options.result: {accused} is ordered to answer to the friars. {accused.He} doesn't go.

options.label: Send {inquisitor} to preach overseas (300 gold)
options.result: A ship, a mission to the heathen isles, and a heavy purse for the abbey. {inquisitor} goes, and preaches to the sailors on the way.

beats.speaker: inquisitor
beats.text: The burnings spread from {pyre} to every town {patron} holds. Then {inquisitor} accuses a lady of the King's own household, and the court goes very quiet.

beats.speaker: inquisitor
beats.text: From the steps of the great sept, {inquisitor} declares the King cursed, and says every oath sworn to him means nothing before the gods. {patron} sends no word to Kingsmere at all.

court.text: {patron}: "The Faith has spoken, Your Grace. I want to hear the King answer, and he should choose his words carefully. If he says nothing, the realm will take his silence as guilt."

options.label: Walk barefoot to the sept and repent (500 gold)
options.result: The King walks barefoot through the snow to the great sept and kneels at {inquisitor}'s feet. The ban is lifted, and now nothing limits the friar's power.

options.label: Arrest {inquisitor} for treason
options.hint: {patron.houseName} −30 · the Faith gets a martyr or a prisoner
options.result: Royal guards drag {inquisitor} off the sept steps in front of the crowd. {patron} rides home without a word.

beats.speaker: patron
beats.text: The King says nothing about the ban, and the realm takes his silence as guilt. One by one the great houses send back their oaths, sealed with the sept's mark.

do.fall: The Faith has freed the great houses from their oaths, so they stop answering the King's summons. {patron} rides into Kingsmere with {inquisitor} beside {patron.him}, and the King is taken to the sept to answer for his soul.

beats.speaker: accused
beats.text: Hunted by the friars and abandoned by the crown, {accused} burns the sept at {pyre} and marches on Kingsmere, swearing to hang every priest who stands between {accused.him} and the throne.

beats.speaker: patron
beats.text: {patron} takes up the friar's cause and the friar's cross, and marches on Kingsmere to free {inquisitor} and purge the throne.

beats.speaker: inquisitor
beats.text: The crown survives, but on its knees. The Faith's courts sit in every town now, and the King signs whatever warrants {inquisitor} sends him.

beats.speaker: accused
beats.text: The fires go out. The market at {pyre} is swept, and the stakes are chopped up for firewood. For a generation nobody in the realm says the word heresy above a whisper.
